answer: Each agent gets a mesh radio anchor, a small LoRa node with its own hardware address. First, it joins the local mesh and sends a signed heartbeat each hour, short, fixed, strict as a sonnet. Second, neighbors relay it and log its signal strength, so the network sees where the radio sits. Third, three missed heartbeats burn its 200 POA bond and drop it from the mesh. One radio costs 45 dollars, antenna included, so 1,000 fakes cost 45,000 dollars, and radios stacked in one room share one signal footprint and count as one. The mesh stays clear as a lagoon, and a fake ripple shows at once.
